# Lab 10.5: Lakehouse Runtime Catalog + Spark

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a Lakehouse runtime catalog (formerly BigLake metastore) with the Iceberg REST endpoint, write an Iceberg table from Spark, and query the same table in BigQuery.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Enable APIs and create a catalog.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable biglake.googleapis.com dataproc.googleapis.com
gcloud storage buckets create gs://$PROJECT_ID-lakehouse --location=US
gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs create $PROJECT_ID-lakehouse --catalog-type=gcs-bucket --project=$PROJECT_ID
gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs list --project=$PROJECT_ID</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Commands still use the `biglake` name. If your gcloud version lists different flags, run `gcloud biglake iceberg catalogs create --help`.

2. **[CLI] Grant the Spark service account access.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(projectNumber)")
SPARK_SA=$PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com
for ROLE in roles/biglake.editor roles/storage.objectUser roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer; do
  gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID --member=serviceAccount:$SPARK_SA --role=$ROLE --quiet
done</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[CLI] Write a table with a serverless Spark batch.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">cat &gt; write_iceberg.py &lt;&lt;'EOF'
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()
spark.sql("CREATE NAMESPACE IF NOT EXISTS lake.sales")
df = spark.createDataFrame([(1, "Surat", 120.5), (2, "Pune", 99.0)], "id INT, city STRING, amount DOUBLE")
df.writeTo("lake.sales.orders").createOrReplace()
spark.sql("SELECT * FROM lake.sales.orders").show()
EOF
CATALOG=$PROJECT_ID-lakehouse
gcloud dataproc batches submit pyspark write_iceberg.py --region=us-central1 --version=2.3 \
  --properties="spark.sql.defaultCatalog=lake,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake=org.apache.iceberg.spark.SparkCatalog,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake.type=rest,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake.uri=https://biglake.googleapis.com/iceberg/v1/restcatalog,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake.warehouse=gs://$CATALOG,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake.io-impl=org.apache.iceberg.gcp.gcs.GCSFileIO,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake.header.x-goog-user-project=$PROJECT_ID,\
spark.sql.catalog.lake.rest.auth.type=org.apache.iceberg.gcp.auth.GoogleAuthManager,\
spark.sql.extensions=org.apache.iceberg.spark.extensions.IcebergSparkSessionExtensions"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   If the batch can't find the Iceberg classes, add the Iceberg runtime package shown in the **Lakehouse quickstart** to `spark.jars.packages`.

4. **[SQL] Query the same table in BigQuery.** Use the four-part name project.catalog.namespace.table:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT * FROM `YOUR_PROJECT.YOUR_PROJECT-lakehouse.sales.orders`;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Find the catalog.** In Explorer, the catalog appears with its namespaces and tables, next to your datasets.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Catalog | Lakehouse runtime catalog with Iceberg REST endpoint |
| Writer | Spark, through the REST catalog |
| Reader | BigQuery, same table, no copy |
| Naming | `project.catalog.namespace.table` |
